baseline-first.note: Set B captures the key engineering facts A omits: the horizontal louvered configuration, the closing/rotational mechanism, and the energy claims (latent solar energy drives the rotation with no additional energy sources). Set A instead repeats the 20% glazing figure four or five times in slightly different bindings, including one with the wrong condition ('of the HARVEST SCREEN') and one vague truncated variant ('of the HARVEST'), plus a spliced quote. B does misbind the 20% figure to the screens' 'operable glazing coverage/composition' twice, but its remaining claims are well bound and its coverage of the actuator and mechanism is substantially more complete and faithful.

variant-first.note: Set A captures the key mechanical facts — horizontal louvered configuration, closing of louvers to shade the south façade, rotational movement driven by a Nitinol wire actuator using the sun's latent energy with no additional energy sources — which Set B omits entirely. Set B is dominated by repeated 20% glazing claims, one of which misattributes the percentage to the HARVEST SCREEN and another with a malformed '20% %' value, plus a trivial rendering claim and a spliced quote. Set A also has flaws (two claims misbinding the 20% glazing share to the screens, a mislabeled 'composition' claim, and an odd Phototrophic condition), but its claims are more numerous, better bound and better supported overall.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures top thickness (0.019 m) and several correct table rows, but it misbinds the 80.8 GPa shear modulus as a "yield strength" and gives the bending/torsional stiffness units as N*m^3 instead of the table's N*m^2 in three claims (TwGJStif, two TwFAStif entries), plus a couple of altered quotes. Set B correctly reports the shear modulus, the 30% thickness increase, the 7,850 kg/m3 baseline density and TMassDen values, but it invents two table entries (TwFAlSef 218.3 N/m and TwFASStiff 614.5 N*m^2) with quotes that appear nowhere on the page and puts TwSSIner 4688.0 in Row 10 when it belongs to the 87.60 m row. Counting all misread/misbound/invented claims, B has fewer errors (3 vs 4) and covers more of the paragraph's key facts, though its two fabrications are the most severe individual failures in either set.

variant-first.note: Set A captures more distinct, correctly bound facts from the page — base diameter and thickness, Young's and shear moduli, the 8,500 kg/m3 effective density with its paint/bolts/welds/flanges rationale, the 7,850 kg/m3 steel reference, the 30% thickness increase, and several correctly keyed Table 6-1 rows (TMassDen, TwEAStif, TwSSStif, TwSSIner) plus the 38.234 m mass center. Set B's table values are mostly right but it repeats the same facts (mass 347,460 kg three times, density three times, Young's modulus twice) and misreads the stiffness unit as N*m^3 in three claims, and it misbinds 80.8 GPa as 'yield strength' when the text calls it the shear modulus. Set A does contain two fabricated table entries (TwFAlSef 218.3 N/m and TwFASStiff 614.5) and one row mislabel (4688.0 kg·m is the 87.60 m row, not 'Row 10'), plus a couple of non-verbatim quote paraphrases. On balance A is the more faithful and better-covered extraction despite those slips.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds the dinner-party guest limit correctly (eight people total — two from each of three neighboring houses plus up to two VIPs) and keeps the 'within a specified period of time' condition and the 0–100% score range, whereas Set A states the guest limit as eight per neighboring house with a fabricated quote. Set A also invents the quote 'the starting water weight shall be 6.00 lb (2.721 kg)' (the source reads 96.00 oz) and offers a vague, unsupported 'linear increase … from 0 to 80 oz' claim backed only by an axis label. Set B does contain one clear error (0 points at 80 oz, where the figure shows full points) and one inferred value (6.000 lb) not stated in the text, but overall it is more faithful and covers the page's key facts better.

variant-first.note: Both sets are heavily redundant, but Set A's core readings are correct: full points at 5.000 lb/80 oz, reduced points between 16 and 80 oz with linear scaling, no points at or below 16 oz/450 g, and the 96.00 oz (2.721 kg) minimum starting weight in a single container. Set A's clear errors are two invented figure readings (claiming 0 points at 80 oz and at 20 oz, when 80 oz is full points and 20 oz is in the reduced range). Set B invents a quote ('starting water weight shall be 6.00 lb'), misstates the guest list as eight people per neighboring house rather than eight total (two from each of three houses plus up to two VIPs), and wrongly describes the scoring function as a linear increase from 0 to 80 oz when it is flat below 16 oz. Set A also captures the Dinner Party score range and guest composition correctly, which Set B gets partly wrong.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds the source values correctly and consistently — 3/4" x 5 1/2" plywood deck and reclaimed wood surface, 2" x 8" frame and joist, 3/4" threaded rod, 1" nut, 4x4 post 'to be cut as needed', FIRST FLR 2'-4" above GRADE LEVEL 0". Set A invents several quotes and values not on the page (5/4" x 6" x 12" pressure treated surfacing, 3/4" x 4' x 8' plywood, 1'-6", 2" SLEEVE) and misstates real ones (2" x 6" joist instead of 2" x 8", 1/2" threaded rod instead of 3/4"). Set B's weaknesses are duplicates and a few vague or misbound dimensions (joist given as 3/4" x 5 1/2", 8'-0" attributed to the footing plan, 4x4 called a footing member), but it has far fewer substantive errors. Set A also misassigns A6/B4 dimensions to the wrong details (1 1/4", 3 3/4", 7 1/2", 8'-0" as Footing Elevation width).

variant-first.note: Set A stays within the page text layer and correctly binds the 3/4" x 5 1/2" plywood/reclaimed wood surface, 2" x 8" frame and joist, 3/8" x 4" hex through bolt, 3/4" threaded rod, 1" nut, 4X4 post and FIRST FLR/GRADE LEVEL elevations. Set B invents several quotes absent from the source (5/4" x 6" x 12" pressure treated surfacing, 3/4" x 4' x 8' plywood, 2" x 6" joist, 1/2" threaded rod, 2" sleeve, 1'-6", 2'-0") and contradicts the text (joist is 2" x 8", rod is 3/4"). B also misbinds 7 1/2" to detail C1 and 8'-0" to Footing Elevation width, and adds vague claims (deck footing height/dimension, assembly width, decking spacing). A's flaws are mainly a few misbound or unsupported bindings (joist given the decking size, footing called 4X4, plan overall width/depth, 'component 1'), but it is clearly more faithful overall.

baseline-first.note: Both sets invent airfoil names not present in the legends (Set A: FFA-W3-1 through -6, SNL-FFA, and a garbled 'SNL-FFA-WFA-W3-500'; Set B: FFA-W3-2, FFA-W3-3, SNL-FFA), and those claims are unsupported. Set B is stronger on the facts that are actually on the page: it captures the Reynolds numbers for all seven legend entries and binds several plausible cl, cd and cl/cd readings to real airfoils, whereas Set A gives only three Re claims and adds four dubious 'cl = 0.0 at AoA = 0' readings (the curves cross cl = 0 at negative angles) plus internally inconsistent peak values for the invented names. Set B does contain a few questionable chart readings (e.g. cl = 2.0 at AoA = 20 for SNL-FFA-W3-500) and contradictory duplicate maxima for the same invented airfoils, but overall it has more correct, well-bound claims and fewer outright fabrications.

variant-first.note: Both sets invent airfoil names not present in the legends (Set A: FFA-W3-3, FFA-W3-2, SNL-FFA; Set B: FFA-W3-1 through FFA-W3-6, plus a misread 'SNL-FFA-WFA-W3-500'), but Set B does so more often and additionally asserts cl = 0.0 at angle of attack 0 deg for four airfoils, which contradicts plot (a) where the curves sit near cl ≈ 0.5–0.8 at 0 deg. Set A correctly captures all seven Reynolds-number legend entries and several plausible readings of the cl/cd peaks and polar points for real airfoils (e.g. FFA-W3-211 peak ≈120, FFA-W3-360 peak ≈75). Set A's errors are mostly its fabricated short-name entities and a couple of questionable cl values, so it is the more faithful set overall.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures the title block metadata (drawn by, checked by, sheet title, sheet number, lot number, copyright) with values and quotes that match the text layer and title block shown in the image. Set B contains no claims at all, so it captures none of the sheet's identifying information. All six of A's claims are supported and correctly bound, so A is clearly better.

variant-first.note: Set A contains no claims at all, so it captures none of the title block information on the page. Set B extracts six title-block fields (drawn by, checked by, sheet title, sheet number, lot number, copyright) with values and quotes that match the text layer and the visible title block. No claim in Set B is misbound or invented, so Set B is clearly better despite the page also containing revision history and project credit data that neither set captured.

baseline-first.note: Set B's wiring-schedule and title-block claims (150 AL 3#4/0/#4G/2-1/2"C, 50 CU 3#6/#8G/1"C, 34 CU 6#10/3#10G/1"C, 33, 32, 31, 20, 10, revisions, lot number, drawn by) all match the page, with only a few vague or truncated items. Set A repeatedly misreads the schedule (Cable 20 as 3#10/1#12G instead of 3#12/#12G, Cable 150 as '3440, 4G', Cable 50 as '3#8, 1#6') and invents two 'Cable 21 / SP100E' entries that do not exist anywhere on the page. Set A also misbinds the NEMA 3R enclosure to MAIN PANEL MP (it belongs to item 6, the 200A/2P NFDS) and adds several trivial or truncated-quote claims ('150', 'CU', 'TO INSTRUME', 'TO UTILI'). B's only real defects are one trivial '50' claim, a truncated 'VOLTAGE ORGANIZE' target, and an unsupported '150 -> SIDE O -> 6' connection claim.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the wiring-schedule entries correctly (150 = AL 3#4/0/#4G/2-1/2"C, 50 = CU 3#6/#8G/1"C, 31–34, 20, 10) and captures the title-block and revision data accurately, with only a trivial '50' claim and two loose diagram claims (invented '150 -> SIDE O -> 6' quote, misread 'VOLTAGE ORGANIZER'). Set B misreads several schedule rows (20 as 3#10/1#12G, 50 as 3#8/1#6, 150 as '3440, 4G'), invents a nonexistent Cable 21 (SP100E), misreads #4G as a '4 G' conductor count, and adds several trivial or truncated claims ('CU', '1', 'TO UTILI', 'TO INSTRUME'). B also drops the N and NO GND conditions from one instrumentation-panel claim, while A keeps them. A is clearly more faithful despite covering fewer facts.

Set A's ten claims are all supported by the page (grade level 0'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", and the 3/8"=1'-0" scales for sections C1/A1), though several are duplicate restatements of the same facts. Set B covers more ground (sheet number A-301, sheet title, per-module finished floor heights) but contains clear errors: it misreads the East Module finished floor as 2' 3 1/2" with a fabricated quote, and twice binds '116' to a lot number even though the text layer shows 'LOT NUMBER:' with no value and 116 only near the scale. Because B invents a value and a field binding while A makes no factual errors, A is the more faithful set despite its redundancy.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures the sheet identity facts (number A-301, title BUILDING SECTIONS, lot number 116) and the section scales, which Set B omits entirely, and it correctly binds the West Module finished-floor height (2' 9 1/2" above grade, Section C1). Set A's main defect is one misread value: the East Module finished-floor height is given as 2' 3 1/2" although the annotation reads 2' - 9 1/2"; Set B states both module conditions correctly. Both sets are padded with duplicate Grade Level / Finished Floor / scale claims, and B also paraphrases scale values ("3/8" 1'-0"", "3/8" per 1'-0""), but B's complete omission of sheet number, title and lot number is a larger loss of important page facts than A's single misread.

variant-first.note: Both sets are dominated by vague entities ('component', 'dimension') that bind real dimension strings to unspecified parts, but Set A includes at least one clearly verifiable and correctly bound claim (Drawing C1 scale 1 1/2" = 1'-0") and correctly ties 3'-1 5/16" and 2'-11 7/8" to the rightmost segments of the Module B and Module A details. Set B misassigns 2'-3 7/8" to Module B when it appears in the Module A detail, truncates 2'-3 7/8" to '2'-3', and invents 'flange width (left/right) 1 1/2"' bindings not supported by the sheet. Set A also has clear errors (4 13" misread of 4 13/16", truncated 2'-3, invented base-block hole offsets and base-plate thickness), so the margin is modest.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are dominated by loosely bound dimension claims, but Set A generally attaches the drawn values to plausible PV structural member features (flange widths, total height 6 13/16", overall length 12'-3 3/4", 1'-11 1/8" support height) and keeps the Module A/B context. Set B adds a valid scale claim and some reasonable segment lengths, but it invents hole/base-block conditions not evidenced in the text layer and misreads 4 13/16" as "4 13" and 2'-3 7/8" as "2'-3". Set A also truncates 2'-3 7/8" to "2'-3" and mislabels the 5/8" dimension as a structural member height. Overall Set A has fewer clear misreadings and better-bound values.

variant-first.note: Set A covers more of the page's key facts correctly, including the Region 3 torque-controller saturation, the pitch-to-feather action to hold rated rotor speed, the tip-deflection/tower-clearance design constraint, the force decrease toward the tip, and the sharp linear drop over the outboard 5% from the Prandtl tip-loss model. Set B mislabels TSR = 8.5 as the design point (the design point is TSR = 9.0, 8.5 is the optimum) and attaches an unsupported 'set point tip-speed ratio' condition to the design-point TSR = 9.0 and pitch = 0° claims. Set A's main flaws are one misbinding (calling the ~90 m force peak a 'peak deflection' location) and one claim with a fabricated, misbound quote ('The design point for this pitch Θpitch = 0°'), plus heavy redundancy of the 4° pitch claim. Overall A is more complete and more faithful.

baseline-first.note: Set B covers the page's key facts more completely — Region 3 torque saturation and pitch-to-feather, the tip-deflection/tower-clearance design constraints, the force decrease toward the tip, and the sharp drop over the outboard 5% — all of which Set A omits. Set A's main substantive error is binding TSR = 8.5 to the 'design point' (the design point is TSR = 9.0; 8.5 is the optimum), plus two claims whose 'set point tip-speed ratio' condition is not supported by the quoted design-point sentence. Set B's errors are one clear misbinding (90 m as 'peak deflection location' when the text says peak aerodynamic force) and one stitched, non-verbatim quote for the design-point pitch, with some redundant repeats of the 4° claim. On balance B is more faithful and far better in coverage despite its one misbound property.

Both sets repeat the same core facts heavily and both mangle the louver height formula (dropping the tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar…) terms and presenting 'Depth * (azimuth – window azimuth)' as a valid formula), but Set A does so more often and additionally mislabels D*1.2 as a spacing/depth-to-height ratio of 1.2 and invents an 'average' condition for the 25-degree bend. Set B adds correctly bound facts Set A omits (powder-coated finish, screen-level louver profile/shape) and keeps the 1:1 depth-to-height ratio and 50-degree solar altitude with their conditions. Set B's weaknesses are mostly garbled or truncated quotes and one fabricated quote ('the extruded louver profile was…'), whereas Set A contains more substantively wrong value/property bindings.

variant-first.note: Both sets repeat the same core facts (50° solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, 0° window azimuth, 1:1 depth-to-height spacing, 25° structural bend, truncated isosceles triangle profile), but Set B garbles the governing formula four times by dropping tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth – window azimuth) and also asserts a 'depth-to-height ratio 1.2' that contradicts the stated 1:1 ratio, plus an invented 'average' condition on the bend. Set A keeps the full formula in at least one claim, adds the powder-coated finish and correct shape/finish bindings, and its main defects are truncated or paraphrased quotes (e.g. 'louver hern azimuth', '50 sing the fall equinox') and two mis-stated formula claims. Set A therefore has fewer substantive misreadings and better coverage, though both sets are heavily duplicated and contain misbound 'spacing formula' claims.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures the page's non-table facts correctly — rated rotor speed 12.1 rpm, rated mechanical power 5.296610 MW, and both forms of the pitch-sensitivity model (Eq. 7-16a/7-16b) — while Set B omits all of these and instead emits four trivial 'row X / column Y' cell claims plus one misbound claim (23.0 m/s wind speed labeled as blade-pitch angle). Both sets share the same class of table error: values written without the E+6 exponent or truncated to a bare 'E', and each has one misread number (A: -83.04E+6 vs -83.94E+6; B: -113.40E+6 vs -114.30E+6). Because A keeps the needed conditions and the important rated-power/rating facts and adds fewer vague or misbound claims, it is the better set despite its exponent omissions.

variant-first.note: Both sets show the same systematic artifact of truncating the E+6 exponent in table values, but Set A additionally invents -113.40E+6 for the 23.0 m/s row (table: -114.30E+6), misbinds 23.0 m/s as a blade-pitch angle, and pads its list with four trivial 'row/column value' claims plus several duplicates. Set B's only substantive numeric error is -83.04E+6 for the 18.0 m/s row (table: -83.94E+6), and it correctly captures Equations 7-16a and 7-16b, the rated mechanical power 5.296610 MW and the rated rotor speed 12.1 rpm, all of which Set A omits. Row coverage of Table 7-1 is comparable (each set drops three rows), so B's additional correct model and rated-value claims and its fewer trivial claims make it the better set despite one more truncated-value claim.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures the key quantitative facts correctly, including the 97:1 gearbox ratio, the 670–871 rpm Region 1½ range, the 6.9 rpm minimum rotor speed, and the peak power coefficient 0.482 at tip-speed ratio 7.55 and 0.0° pitch at 8 m/s. Set B misreads several values (97.1:1 gear ratio, 5.298610 MW rated mechanical power instead of 5.296610 MW, a spurious '1.963 rpm' rated speed) and misbinds the fourth-order state-space statement to the baseline filter and the 6.9 rpm rotor speed to the generator. Set A's flaws are minor: one claim drops the squared unit (Nm/rpm), one leaves the tip-speed ratio unspecified, and two quotes omit 'filtered' from the speed term. Overall A is substantially more faithful and complete.

variant-first.note: Set B binds the key quantities more faithfully: it correctly reports the 97:1 gearbox ratio, the 0.0255764 N·m/rpm² Region 2 constant (in one claim with the right unit), the 6.9 rpm minimum rotor speed as a rotor (not generator) property, and the peak Cp of 0.482 at TSR 7.55, 0.0° pitch, 8 m/s. Set A introduces clear misreads and misbindings: 97.1:1 instead of 97:1, rated mechanical power 5.298610 MW instead of 5.296610 MW, an invented rated speed of 1.963 rpm, the rotor's 6.9 rpm bound to the generator, the fourth-order state-space note bound to the baseline filter (it applies to the alternative filters considered), and a quote with fabricated '[missing]' text, plus heavy duplication. B's weaknesses are a wrong unit (Nm/rpm) on one constant claim, two claims that drop 'filtered' from the speed relationship, and omission of the rated mechanical power (5.296610 MW) and rated generator speed (1173.7 rpm) that A does capture. On balance B has more unique correct claims and far fewer substantive errors.

baseline-first.note: Both sets mix sound text-derived claims with shaky readings of Figure 7-2, but Set B captures more of the page's key facts (high drivetrain structural damping, single-DOF design model, gain-scheduled PI blade-pitch control, Region 2½ span) that Set A omits. Set A's worst items are fabricated or nonsensical: it reports the torque rate limit as 'not specified' with an invented '[value missing]' quote although the text gives 15,000 N·m/s, binds 1173.7 rpm to 'filtered generator speed' instead of rated generator speed, and gives garbled 'torque response' values (~1100 at 1150 rpm, ~900 at 1400 rpm). Set B's errors are mainly non-faithful truncated quotes for the 47,402.91 N·m saturation, one misbinding ('actual speed' vs. filtered speed), and a wrong Region 1½ speed span (700–900 rpm vs. ~650–850 rpm from the figure). Both sets contain duplicated and axis-label-only trivial claims, but B is the more faithful set overall.

variant-first.note: Set A captures the page's textual facts faithfully — the 47,402.91 N·m (10% above rated) torque saturation, the 15,000 N·m/s rate limit, the 1° previous blade-pitch-command trigger, the 1173.7 rpm rated speed, the gain-scheduled PI pitch control and single-DOF design model, plus the high drivetrain damping. Set B invents a 'not specified' rate limit when the text explicitly gives 15,000 N·m/s (contradicting its own later claim), misbinds 1173.7 rpm to 'filtered generator speed' rather than rated speed, and contains two nonsensical 'approx 1100/900 not specified' claims. Set A's weaknesses are a handful of graph claims with unsupported or fabricated quote text (e.g. 'Optimal [black line] intersection…'), one garbled saturation quote, and one claim that calls the speed 'actual' instead of 'filtered'; Set B also omits the PI/single-DOF design facts and has mutually inconsistent endpoint values (35,000 vs 36,000 N·m at 1400 rpm).

Set A binds the wiring-schedule symbols to their conductor specs correctly (20→3#12/#12G, 50→3#6/#8G, 150→AL 3#4/0, 32→2#10USE-2, 33/34→6#10 variants) and correctly reads the notes (50A/2P main breaker, 200A/2P NFDS, 60A DC NFDS, NEMA 3R enclosures, junction box, revisions, lot number). Set B makes a serious misbinding by assigning the 200A/2P rating to the SUB-PANEL main breaker (the note gives 50A/2P; 200A/2P is the NFDS), downgrades NEMA 3R to "NEMA 3" twice, and introduces three wire specs (101, 105, 106) that appear nowhere on the page. Set A's flaws are a garbled/misbound "MAIN BREAKER ... WITH GROUND FAULT" quote (ground fault belongs to the 2.8kW inverter) and an unsupported "component 2 connected to ground" claim. Set B does capture the 120/240V sub-panel voltage and the 60A DC NFDS, but its invented and misbound claims outweigh that.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds the wiring-schedule rows to the correct symbol numbers (20, 31, 32, 33, 34, 50, 150, 151, 10) and correctly reads the notes and title-block facts (200A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R junction box and sub-panel enclosure, lot number 113, revisions 03/04). Set A invents three wire specifications (101, 105, 106 – 'CU #10, STR', 'MIN R=3.0"') that appear nowhere in the text layer, misbinds the 200A/2P rating to the SUB-PANEL main breaker (which the notes give as 50A/2P), and repeatedly misquotes 'NEMA 3R' as 'NEMA 3' and 'NFDS' as 'NPDFS'. A does capture a few facts B omits (60A DC NFDS, 120/240V, 2P main breaker), but its errors are substantive misreadings and fabrications, while B's flaws are mainly vague entities, a garbled 'ground fault' claim bound to the main breaker instead of the inverter, and an unsupported '4 connected to 31' link.
